extraction.methodology_summary: The strategy models the term structure of VIX futures using a stationary vector autoregressive (VAR) process centered around its mode. A deep feed-forward neural network with five hidden layers is trained on simulated data from the VAR model to maximize expected day-ahead utility over a discrete action space of rolling VIX futures allocations. The model's out-of-sample performance is tested using a 10-fold cross-validation procedure across historical daily data.
extraction.universe: One-month, two-month, three-month, fourth-month, five-month, and six-month VIX futures contracts

key_findings: VIX futures curves are shown to be stationary and possess a strong propensity to revert to contango, making them suitable for tactical trading strategies.
Utilizing a deep feed-forward neural network to approximate day-ahead expected utility yields robust out-of-sample trading signals with high positive returns and Sharpe ratios.
The neural network-based trading signals outperform constant benchmark trading allocations and individual static strategies across almost all cross-validation folds.

While the strategy delivers considerable profits, it also exhibits high maximum drawdowns which can be challenging to manage in practice, and portfolio performance declines as transaction costs are introduced.
limitations: Maximum drawdowns remain high throughout backtests, posing practical management challenges.
Performance degrades as the transaction cost basis points parameter in the execution model increases.
